response.sql: SELECT AVG(CASE WHEN amount > 0 THEN spent / amount END) as avg_ratio, COUNT(*) as line_count FROM budget WHERE spent >= 6.0

assumptions.assumption: The count 'how many such lines are there' refers to all budget lines where spent >= 6.0, regardless of whether their ratio can be calculated. The phrase 'ignoring missing ratios' applies only to the average calculation. Missing ratios are those where amount is 0 or NULL (making division impossible).

alternatives.interpretation: If 'such lines' is interpreted as only those budget lines with a calculable ratio (amount > 0), then the count should exclude rows where the ratio is missing.
alternatives.sql: SELECT AVG(CASE WHEN amount > 0 THEN spent / amount END) as avg_ratio, COUNT(CASE WHEN amount > 0 THEN 1 END) as line_count FROM budget WHERE spent >= 6.0
